_readme: Draft eval set for the PKA sample corpus. Questions marked in 'notes' were written from knowledge of the papers: check them against the PDFs. Temporal ground truth is in eval/version_changes.md.

questions.question: How much security deposit did I pay for the flat, and how soon do I get it back after moving out?
questions.expected_answer: ₹84,000 (three months' fee), refunded within 30 days of vacating, minus unpaid dues and damage.

questions.question: What are the quiet hours in my housing society?
What cost per acquisition is Brewbox aiming for?
questions.expected_answer: Under ₹330 per new subscriber.

questions.question: What security rules do Northwind employees have to follow when working from home?
questions.expected_answer: Use the company VPN on every remote day, no public Wi-Fi for confidential work, and lock the screen when stepping away.

questions.question: Can someone at Northwind work remotely from another country?
questions.expected_answer: No. Working from outside India is not permitted, for tax and data-protection reasons.

questions.question: Which model am I using to find chunk boundaries, and which one for the final embeddings?
questions.expected_answer: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for sentence-level boundary detection; bge-base-en for the final chunk embeddings.

questions.question: How many dimensions does bge-base-en produce?
How many pressure cooker whistles does my dal need?
questions.expected_answer: 3 whistles, because the dal is soaked for 20 minutes first (otherwise 5).

questions.question: How much is the scooter rental in Goa?
questions.expected_answer: ₹500 per day, arranged through the guesthouse.

questions.question: What percentile threshold was I using for chunk boundaries in the design review, and what did Rohan suggest?
questions.expected_answer: The 92nd percentile; Rohan suggested comparing 90 and 95 on the eval.

questions.question: How much faster is Sentence-BERT than plain BERT at finding the most similar pair in 10,000 sentences?
questions.expected_answer: From about 65 hours with BERT to about 5 seconds with SBERT.

questions.question: How many attention heads does the base Transformer model use?
questions.expected_answer: 8 heads, with a model dimension of 512.

questions.question: What are the four core functions in the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
questions.expected_answer: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.

questions.question: Where in a long prompt do language models make the best use of relevant information?
questions.expected_answer: At the beginning or the end of the context; performance drops when it sits in the middle.

questions.question: What are the two variants of the original RAG model and how do they differ?
questions.expected_answer: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved passages for the whole output; RAG-Token can use different passages for each generated token.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the RAPTOR paper?
questions.expected_answer: Build a tree by recursively clustering text chunks and summarising each cluster, then retrieve across tree levels, which helps questions that need broad or multi-part context.

questions.question: How is the big survey of large language models organised?
questions.expected_answer: Around pre-training, adaptation (instruction tuning and alignment), utilisation (prompting, in-context learning, chain of thought) and capacity evaluation, plus resources.

questions.question: How does the Gao et al. survey categorise RAG systems?
questions.expected_answer: Into Naive RAG, Advanced RAG and Modular RAG, and it reviews retrieval, generation, augmentation and evaluation.

questions.question: What does the NIST Generative AI Profile cover overall?
questions.expected_answer: Risks that generative AI creates or worsens (such as confabulation, information integrity, privacy, harmful bias and IP) and suggested actions mapped onto the AI RMF functions.

questions.question: What themes keep coming up across my PKA meetings, the design-review call and my brain-dump?
questions.expected_answer: Structure-first chunking with semantic splitting only where needed; the move to Qdrant and bge-base-en; honest evaluation reported per document type; keeping summarisation cost down; and Rohan's reranker notes.

questions.question: How has my thinking on chunk boundaries developed over time?
questions.expected_answer: From plain semantic splitting to headings and clauses as hard boundaries, a continuity penalty for connective sentences, windowed comparisons, testing several percentile thresholds, and keeping short notes as single chunks.

questions.question: What are my main obligations as the tenant under the rental agreement?
questions.expected_answer: Pay the fee on time, pay utilities, use the flat only as a residence without subletting, handle my share of repairs, follow society rules, give written notice and return the flat in good condition.

questions.question: Summarise Brewbox's Q3 marketing strategy.
questions.expected_answer: Launch the Single Origin Club tier, drive sign-ups mainly through paid social plus search, measure cost per acquisition and retention, and shift budget monthly based on results.

questions.question: What have I read so far for this project and what's still on my list?
questions.expected_answer: Read: the RAG paper and Sentence-BERT. Skimmed: DPR and Lost in the Middle. To read: RAPTOR (top priority for Phase 4), the Gao survey and the NIST AI RMF.

questions.question: How do Dense Passage Retrieval and the original RAG paper each use retrieval?
questions.expected_answer: DPR trains a dual-encoder retriever that beats BM25 for open-domain QA; RAG pairs a DPR-style retriever with a BART generator and trains them together for generation.

questions.question: What is my monthly rent now?
questions.expected_answer: ₹30,240 per month.

questions.question: What was my rent in June 2026?
questions.expected_answer: ₹28,000 per month.

questions.question: How did the rule on who pays for repairs change in the renewed agreement?
questions.expected_answer: The minor-versus-major split was replaced by a cost threshold: I pay for any repair under ₹2,000, the owner pays for ₹2,000 or more unless I caused the damage, and a quote is needed first.

questions.question: What changed overall when the rental agreement was renewed?
questions.expected_answer: New term Dec 2026–Oct 2027; rent ₹28,000 to ₹30,240; late fee ₹500 to ₹750 a day; parking clause removed and a pets clause added; repairs rule rewritten; notice one month to two months; renewal cap 5% to 8%.

questions.question: How many days a week can Northwind employees work from home?
questions.expected_answer: Up to three days a week.

questions.question: What was the Northwind internet allowance in July 2026?
questions.expected_answer: ₹1,000 per month.

questions.question: What happened to the rule about being in the office on Fridays?
questions.expected_answer: It was removed in the October 2026 policy and replaced by core hours of 11:00 to 16:00 IST.

questions.question: What was the Q3 marketing budget and its split as of the end of July?
questions.expected_answer: ₹4,00,000: paid social 60%, search 25%, influencers 15%.

questions.question: How and why did the Q3 marketing plan change mid-quarter?
questions.expected_answer: Budget cut to ₹3,20,000, target lowered to 1,000 after a slow July, launch moved to 1 August due to a packaging delay, and influencers replaced by webinars and email because creator codes converted poorly.

questions.question: What changed between the draft and the approved PKA proposal?
questions.expected_answer: MiniLM and Chroma became bge-base-en and Qdrant; 10 weeks became 12; budget ₹3,000 to ₹5,000 a month; target hit@5 0.80 to 0.85; the mobile-app stretch goal was dropped and a Risks section added.
